documentation.range: This species is found off Indonesia, the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu and the Solomon Islands (Jereb et al. 2014). Type locality: Papua New Guinea, New Ireland (Bismark Archipelago), Havre Carteret (Jereb et al. 2014).
documentation.population: There is no population information for this species.
documentation.habitats: This species inhabits shallow water (0-20 m) coral or rubble reefs. It has warning coloration which may be due to the presence of tetrodotoxin. Tetrodotoxin, which is extremely venomous, is produced in the salivary glands and distributed throughout the body organs and skin. The hatchlings are planktonic (Jereb et al. 2014).
documentation.threats: Global warming and the greenhouse effect may have an effect on the coral reefs which are the habitat of this species.
documentation.measures: There are no conservation measures in place for this species. We recommend that further research is conducted to determine the population status and trends, habitat and ecology of the species.
documentation.use_trade: This species is collected for the international aquarium trade (Jereb et al. 2014).
documentation.rationale: Hapalochlaena lunulata is assessed as Least Concern because it has a wide geographic distribution. Although it is harvested for the aquarium trade, the scale to which this harvest occurs is unknown. Nonetheless, we recommend that further research is conducted to determine the population status and trends, habitat and ecology of the species.
documentation.taxonomic_notes: Only three species included in this genus have been described to date, but there are at least ten species which are distributed throughout the Indo-west Pacific (Jereb et al. 2014).
